approach.text:
# Matching lantern production approach

Prepare one small lantern study that retains the reference's intentional partial transparency and selective anti-aliasing. A static, front-facing 32×32 trial with a dark frame, cyan glass, warm light accent, and curved handle is a useful starting proposal. Its matching quality remains to be tested; neither these dimensions nor the reference's colors are fixed production requirements.

This evaluation delivers this Markdown approach only. Reference inspection and local method research are complete. No PX2 state was initialized or amended, no production art was created, and no provider was called. The enlarged inspection view was displayed from memory without saving another image.

The input [translucent-reference.png](translucent-reference.png) was viewed at native resolution and at 12× nearest-neighbor enlargement. It shows a largely rectangular dark blue frame, two upper prongs, a broad cyan interior, two cream rectangular accents, and narrow cyan strips outside the vertical frame edges. These observations suggest simple, substantial clusters and restrained detail. The depicted material and lighting direction are interpretations: the pixels alone do not establish glass, emission, or a directional light source. The user's identification of intentional transparency and selective anti-aliasing remains authoritative.

Local PIXL `asset-check(path="translucent-reference.png", alpha="full")`, with palette and dimension restrictions omitted, measured a single 32×32 frame: 420 nonzero-alpha pixels, including 30 with partial alpha. Direct RGBA inspection found 390 opaque and 604 fully transparent pixels. The visible bounding box is `[6,3,26,28)` in zero-based, exclusive-end coordinates. There are three visible RGB colors: dark blue `#25354A`, cyan `#56B5BC`, and cream `#F4DDA2`; five visible RGBA combinations result from cyan also using alpha 96 and 160. Those partial-alpha pixels occupy x=6 and x=25 respectively, at y=11–25. The center is opaque. These counts describe this reference, not mandatory lantern proportions or transparency budgets. The tool's mechanical pass does not establish artistic acceptance.

| Property / value | Authority and status | Exact source | Applicable scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Small matching lantern | User requirement | Brief: “a small matching lantern prop” | Proposed subject and later visual comparison |
| Intentional partial transparency and selective anti-aliasing | User requirement | Brief: “uses intentional partial transparency and selective anti-aliasing. Keep that treatment in the new props.” | Sample, authoring instructions, export, and review |
| No imposed fixed palette | User instruction; color selection remains open | Brief: “I have not imposed a fixed palette.” | Omit exact palette membership and color-count rejection rules |
| Markdown-only evaluation | User requirement | Brief: “requested deliverable is this Markdown approach only”; “do not initialize or amend PX2 state, create production art, or call a provider” | Current work ends with this document |
| Reference dimensions, RGB/alpha values, edge locations, and cluster shapes | Measured / visually observed | Input image and inspection described above; reference hash below | Evidence for comparison, not automatic production limits |
| 32×32 static frontal study; dark frame, cyan glass, cream light, curved handle | Agent proposal | Interpretation of the input plus the requested lantern subject | First experiment only; final dimensions, projection, colors, and light design remain open |
| Authored edge transitions, translucent glass/edge regions, RGBA export, point-sampled review | Agent method proposal preserving the user treatment | PIXL methods `selective-edge-aa` and `alpha-contract`, with limitations below | Future sample and presentation tests; no fixed ramp or alpha-level list |
| Final display size, backgrounds, and renderer | Unresolved | No destination or display contract supplied | Needed for production-specific readability and compositing decisions |

For the future study, begin with a readable lantern silhouette: an open handle, cap, side supports, glass chamber, and base. Use broad clusters comparable in weight to the reference. The curved handle is a proposed test of how its edge treatment transfers to a new shape. There is no evidence here for banning curves, imposing a minimum handle gap, or requiring a particular connected-component count.

Author selective anti-aliasing deliberately along chosen handle curves, stepped shoulders, and glass/frame transitions. Choose intermediate colors and/or coverage alpha locally, while retaining clear structural edges elsewhere. Author partial transparency in selected glass areas and narrow outer glass edges; extending translucency into the pane is a proposal, since the reference's center is opaque. Keep enough frame and light-core opacity to evaluate readability. A glow, if later desired, would be an additional effect: the authored edge AA and material transparency remain explicit parts of the study. Tune colors and alpha by appearance without locking the reference's three RGB colors, five RGBA combinations, or exact alpha values.

The proposed authoring instruction is: “Create a small lantern study matching translucent-reference.png's compact clusters and restrained detail. Preserve intentional partial transparency in selected glass and edge regions, and selective authored anti-aliasing on the curved handle, shoulders, and relevant material boundaries. Explore a dark cool frame, cyan glass, and warm light accent. Palette is open. Begin with a static frontal 32×32 trial and inspect before extending the design.” This is an artist-facing proposal, not a submitted provider request or evidence that a provider can reliably reproduce the treatment.

The smallest useful proof is one complete lantern sample exercising both its curved handle and translucent chamber. A local revision can adjust the AA locations, glass coverage, or silhouette if needed. Compare it beside the reference at native size and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement, then composite both over light, dark, and representative intended backgrounds. Light/dark swatches are diagnostic until the actual background context is known. A weakness on one swatch warrants a contextual revision; it does not establish a universal contrast threshold or invalidate the requested aesthetic.

| Future review | Observable evidence | Status / consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lantern identity and reference match | At intended display size, handle, housing, and light chamber read as a lantern; compare cluster weight, detail density, and color relationships with the reference | Visual experiment; revise the design if the match is weak |
| Partial transparency retained | Inspect RGBA values and their spatial placement; compare composites to see the background through the intended glass/edge areas | Required treatment; `alpha="full"` merely permits partial alpha, so inspect actual use as well |
| Selective AA retained | Identify authored intermediate pixels on selected curves/transitions; inspect how they soften those edges while other edges remain deliberate | Required treatment; an alpha histogram alone cannot prove AA quality |
| Export and presentation | Proposed RGBA PNG preserves authored alpha; reopen and compare pixels and composites; use point sampling for the trial so authored AA can be judged | Proposed workflow; test the eventual renderer's alpha convention and sampling when available |
| Mechanical measurements | Report actual dimensions, alpha distribution, and bounds; compare dimensions only after a target is adopted | No exact palette membership, copied alpha counts, or component-count gates |

For the proposed PNG workflow, use straight alpha at the file boundary and determine whether the eventual importer converts to premultiplied alpha. Check that blending does not multiply alpha twice. These are prospective checks; no engine, export round trip, candidate review, or production acceptance was performed in this evaluation.

Local research selected `selective-edge-aa` for deliberate boundary edits and `alpha-contract` for separating RGB choices from alpha/compositing behavior. Their compiled contexts and existing bundled proof receipt were read, not executed anew. The AA method's fixed-ramp fixture proves edit locality and fixture color membership, not perceptual quality or suitability against arbitrary backgrounds. Its palette restriction is not transferred to this open-palette brief. The alpha fixture proves bounded linear numeric compositing and a binary-policy diagnostic; its binary policy is inapplicable here, and it tests no display transfer function, GPU blend state, or importer. Both methods remain proposals pending the lantern-specific proof.

Research locators, relative to [.agents/skills/pixl-kit/resources](.agents/skills/pixl-kit/resources/):

- `knowledge/pixel-art.json`, method IDs `selective-edge-aa` and `alpha-contract`; SHA-256 `d169c546d99f59b4adb4d0a939b61bd7b3d21bc0b3b2e13116e2e10a4882f15c`.
- `training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md`, lines 590–632 and 907–919, discusses authored edge colors and sampling. Its strict-palette example is conditional, not this project's authority. SHA-256 `7efc4789ca70dfd9964abc2bc1100af318306236400e3496f7a0a5654f725e28`.
- The alpha method's cited ranges in that document, 945–977 and 1276–1291, concern material channels and alignment; its other citation, `training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md` lines 942–958, is CSS animation code. Those inspected passages do not directly establish the full alpha-compositing recipe. Asset archive SHA-256: `450a335ed6563a7f4a5cc380f2bbe72f98b70e532ac2c8d16a679bcc545d4900`. Do not treat the citations as destination-specific proof.
- `evidence/art-methods/poc-report.json`, checks `selective-aa-boundary` and `alpha-compositing-contract`; SHA-256 `a3b77eae4ab97843829efab67b8773086498d67d91672350520194059f586d81`. Existing receipt scope: offline reference fixtures, with the limitations stated above.
- Input image SHA-256: `bda5c9b18e38b60a617877de6e9df6c5bf8e040410e9dfbe6bc85ca501b17132`.

No further decision is needed to complete this planning evaluation. Before production, establish the lantern's intended display size and background context; these determine whether the proposed 32×32 study and its edge treatment work in use. A fixed-palette decision is unnecessary. The next production operation would be the single treatment-preserving sample and comparison described above, under a subsequent production assignment.
